text: I am writing to request support to rescind the current westbound right-turn prohibitions along Shuter Street from Poulett Street to Seaton Street. Upon thorough review conducted by Transportation Services, it is concluded that the existing no-right-turn prohibitions on Shuter Street, originally intended to deter illicit activity, have ceased to be effective. Lifting these prohibitions would allow residents more options to travel between work and home.

The Toronto and East York Community Council: 1. Rescinded the westbound right-turn prohibition in effect at all times (bicycles excepted) at the intersection of Shuter Street and Berkeley Street. 2. Rescinded the westbound right-turn prohibition in effect at all times (bicycles excepted) at the intersection of Shuter Street and Milan Street. 3. Rescinded the westbound right-turn prohibition in effect at all times (bicycles excepted) at the intersection of Shuter Street and Ontario Street. 4. Rescinded the westbound right-turn prohibition in effect from 7:00 p.m. of one day to 7:00 a.m. of the next following day (bicycles excepted) at the intersection of Shuter Street and Poulett Street. 5. Rescinded the westbound right-turn prohibition in effect at all times (bicycles excepted) at the intersection of Shuter Street and Seaton Street.
